title: This North Shore city was Realtor.com’s hottest ZIP code in 2026
author: Annie Jonas
bullets: Peabody, Massachusetts named the hottest ZIP code by Realtor.com in 2026, marking its third top-10 appearance.
Peabody listings received 4.1 times the national average views and sold in 20 days, faster than the 60-day national average.
Peabody's median listing price was $667,000 in June, below Boston's metro median but $230,000 above the national average.

title: Q&A: A 96-year-old traveler on visiting all 63 national parks with her grandson
author: Kristi Palma
bullets: Brad and Joy Ryan visited all 63 U.S. national parks from 2015 to 2023.
Joy Ryan, 96, is the oldest person to visit all national parks, completing the journey in the National Park of American Samoa.
The pair will share their experiences and memoir at Harvard Book Store on August 13 during their book tour.

title: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel shares what he’s learned from offseason counseling​
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Mike Vrabel discussed the importance of counseling for personal and team improvement during the 2026 Patriots season.
Vrabel missed a day of the 2026 NFL Draft to attend family counseling, amid reports regarding Dianna Russini.
Vrabel emphasizes balancing family and football, highlighting ongoing mental fitness efforts within the Patriots organization.

title: Worcester officials urge MBTA to improve commuter rail service to and from Boston
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Worcester officials urge MBTA to restore express rail service, aiming for 55-60 minute trips between Worcester and Boston.
Worcester MBTA Working Group's report addresses travel time, infrastructure upgrades, and potential bottlenecks at Boston's Allston Multimodal Project.
Framingham/Worcester Line, highly used by commuters, faces challenges including mechanical disruptions, signal system upgrades, and expanding service to 80 trains by 2035.

title: One of the rarest basketball cards in the world was pulled in New England on Monday
author: Lauren Daley
bullets: A 1:1 Cooper Flagg Rookie Debut Patch Autograph card was pulled by RhodyBreakers in North Kingstown, Rhode Island.
The rare basketball card, featuring Flagg's debut jersey patch, is estimated to be worth $2-5 million.
The Dallas Mavericks offered tickets and memorabilia for the card, but collectors suggest holding for a higher cash offer.

title: Review & setlist: Olivia Dean taught Boston how to love at TD Garden
author: Kelly Chan
bullets: Olivia Dean performed at TD Garden in Boston on August 10, highlighting songs from her album 'The Art of Loving'.
The concert featured a soulful mix of jazzy ballads and emotional performances, with Dean emphasizing themes of love and self-discovery.
The show included crowd favorites like 'Dive' and 'Man I Need', culminating in a pink confetti finale.

title: Belmont, Mass., teens arrested after N.H. police chase
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Two 18-year-olds from Belmont, Massachusetts, were arrested after a high-speed chase in New Hampshire ended with their capture.
Driver Justin Jedrey faced multiple charges, including felony reckless conduct, while passenger Nikol Muka faced intoxication charges.
Jedrey is held in preventive detention, with a court date on Aug. 20, while Muka was released on bail for a Sept. 28 hearing.

title: Faneuil Hall managers sue tenants over more than $2 million in alleged unpaid rent
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Faneuil Hall managers filed lawsuits against seven tenants for over $2 million in alleged unpaid rent and fees.
J. Safra Real Estate, managing since 2024, is improving the site amid legal actions and vacant storefronts.
Boston Mayor held a workshop with experts to explore new directions for the historic Faneuil Hall Marketplace.

title: Do you really need a 4-year degree to build a career in Mass.?
author: Pattie Hunt Sinacole
bullets: Rising college costs and employer shifts are influencing the necessity of a 4-year degree in Massachusetts.
Healthcare and trades offer career paths without requiring a bachelor's degree, with significant demand expected through 2034.
Massachusetts provides alternative education routes like community college certificates and vocational training for various careers.

title: Mike Vrabel: Drake Maye is not expected to play in preseason opener
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: Patriots quarterback Drake Maye is not expected to play in the preseason opener against the Colts.
New England held a joint practice with the Colts for starters to gain reps without game contact.
Backup quarterbacks Tommy DeVito and rookie Behren Morton will have increased opportunities in the preseason.
